description: JACL Lexer (Milestone 1) - Streaming tokenizer for Phase 1 bracket syntax, producing an arena-allocated token array from byte buffer input

userStories.title: Define token types and lexer data structures
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the token enum, Token struct, and lexer API defined in a single-header library so that all subsequent stories can build on a stable interface.
acceptanceCriteria: lexer/lexer.h exists following single-header convention (#ifdef LEXER_IMPLEMENTATION guard)

TokenType enum includes: LBRACKET, RBRACKET, LBRACE, RBRACE, LPAREN, RPAREN, WORD, OPERATOR, KEYWORD, INT, FLOAT, STRING, STRING_BEGIN, STRING_PART, STRING_END, INTERP_VAR, INTERP_EXPR_START, INTERP_EXPR_END, VAR, DOLLAR_BRACKET, NEWLINE, ERROR, EOF_TOKEN

Token struct contains: TokenType type, uint32_t line, uint32_t column, uint32_t offset, uint32_t length, and a union payload (const char* text pointer, int32_t int_val, float float_val, const char* error_msg)
LexResult struct contains: Token* tokens, uint32_t count, uint32_t error_count
Public API function declared: LexResult lexer_lex(const char* source, arena_t* arena)
Header includes only arena/arena.h and platform/platform.h
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Lex delimiters, whitespace, newlines, and EOF
userStories.description: As the parser, I need bracket/brace/paren tokens, newline tokens, and EOF so that the basic structure of JACL programs can be parsed.
acceptanceCriteria: Each of [ ] { } ( ) produces the correct distinct token type
Spaces and tabs are skipped (no tokens emitted)
\n produces a NEWLINE token; \r\n produces a single NEWLINE token
Consecutive newlines produce consecutive NEWLINE tokens
End of input produces an EOF_TOKEN as the final token
All tokens carry correct line, column, and byte offset
lexer/test_lexer.c exists and is added to TESTS array in build.sh
Tests use test/test_helpers.h with tracked_allocator plugged into the arena
Zero memory leaks under tracked allocator
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Lex comments, bare words, operators, and keywords
userStories.description: As the parser, I need word tokens for command names/arguments, operator tokens for symbolic operators, keyword tokens for map keys, and comments skipped.
acceptanceCriteria: # starts a line comment — everything from # to end of line is skipped, no token emitted
A comment before a newline still produces the NEWLINE token
Sequences of letter/digit/underscore/hyphen/UTF-8 characters produce WORD tokens
Sequences of operator characters (!%&*+-./<=>?@\^|~) produce OPERATOR tokens
Colon followed by word characters (e.g. :key, :my-thing) produces KEYWORD tokens
Token payload text pointer points into original source buffer with correct length
Bare words terminate at whitespace, delimiters ([]{}()), $, ", #, or EOF
Tests cover: simple words, UTF-8 words, operators, keywords, comments before/after tokens, mixed sequences
Zero memory leaks under tracked allocator
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Lex numeric literals
userStories.description: As the parser, I need integer and float tokens so that numeric values can be compiled to constants.
acceptanceCriteria: Decimal integer literals (42, 0) produce INT tokens
Float literals (3.14, 0.5) produce FLOAT tokens
Hex literals (0xFF, 0x1A) produce INT tokens
Binary literals (0b1010, 0b0) produce INT tokens
Numbers followed immediately by word characters (42abc) produce an ERROR token
Token payload stores the parsed numeric value (int32_t for INT, float for FLOAT)
Tests cover: zero, positive ints, floats, hex, binary, invalid suffixes, edge cases (INT32_MAX, very small floats)
Zero memory leaks under tracked allocator
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Lex variable references
userStories.description: As the parser, I need $identifier tokens for variable reads and $[ for subcommand expressions.
acceptanceCriteria: $identifier produces a VAR token with payload pointing to the identifier name (without $)
$[ produces a DOLLAR_BRACKET token (parser will handle the expression inside)
$ followed by non-identifier, non-[ character produces an ERROR token with descriptive message
$ at end of input produces an ERROR token
Variable identifiers can contain letters, digits, underscores, hyphens (first char must be letter or underscore)
Tests cover: simple vars ($x, $foo), compound names ($my-var, $foo_bar), $[ token, error cases ($, $123, $!)
Zero memory leaks under tracked allocator
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Lex simple strings (no interpolation)
userStories.description: As the parser, I need double-quoted string tokens with escape sequence handling for literal strings.
acceptanceCriteria: Double-quoted strings with no interpolation ("hello world") produce a single STRING token
Escape sequences handled: \\, \", \n, \t, \r, \0
Hex escapes (\xNN) produce the correct byte value
Unicode escapes (\uNNNN, \UNNNNNNNN) produce valid UTF-8 byte sequences
Invalid escape sequences (e.g. \q) produce an ERROR token, lexing continues after the string
Unterminated strings (missing closing quote) produce an ERROR token at EOF
Strings may contain embedded newlines (multi-line strings)
Escaped content is stored in an arena-allocated buffer (since it differs from source)
Tests cover: empty string, simple string, all escape types, multi-line, unterminated, invalid escapes
Zero memory leaks under tracked allocator
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Lex interpolated strings
userStories.description: As the parser, I need strings with $var and $[expr] interpolation to produce structured token sequences so the parser can build interpolated string AST nodes.
acceptanceCriteria: String with $var interpolation ("hello $name") produces: STRING_BEGIN, INTERP_VAR, STRING_END
String with $[expr] interpolation ("val: $[+ 1 2]") produces: STRING_BEGIN, INTERP_EXPR_START, tokens for expr, INTERP_EXPR_END, STRING_END
STRING_BEGIN/STRING_PART/STRING_END carry the literal text portions of the string
Multiple interpolations in one string produce alternating STRING_PART and INTERP tokens
Nested brackets within $[expr] are handled correctly (lexer tracks bracket depth)
String with no interpolation still produces a single STRING token (not BEGIN/END)
Mixed escape sequences and interpolation in same string work correctly
Tests cover: single var interpolation, single expr interpolation, multiple interpolations, nested brackets in expr, adjacent interpolations, interpolation at start/end of string
Zero memory leaks under tracked allocator
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99

userStories.title: Error recovery and full-program lexing
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the lexer to recover from errors and correctly lex complete multi-line programs so that multiple errors can be reported at once.
acceptanceCriteria: Invalid characters (stray control chars like \x01) produce ERROR tokens with descriptive messages
After an error token, lexing continues from the next recoverable position
Multiple errors in one input all produce separate ERROR tokens with correct positions
LexResult.error_count reflects the total number of ERROR tokens
Error token payload carries an arena-allocated human-readable message string
Full multi-line programs with mixed valid and invalid constructs produce correct token sequences
Position tracking (line, column, offset) remains correct after errors
Integration test: lex a realistic 50+ line JACL program and verify every token
Zero memory leaks under tracked allocator
Compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra -std=c99
